content.thinking: Inspect training features, then submit six selective policies.

All decisions have consumerCount=1. The only rejected decision was ratio ~1.06 (17254224→17549136, ex0 last). Selective policies: use consumer_tree with per-consumer threshold. Since I can't observe consumer features measured, use aggregate features in consumer tree? Consumer tree features include producerWork, consumerWork, fusedConsumerWork etc — I can build tree on fusedConsumerWork <= consumerWork * threshold. But I don't know per-consumer consumerWork. I can write consumer_tree threshold nodes anyway; the compiler computes it. Design: keep aggregate default (e.g., threshold 1.02 or even permissive since selective tree guards), and consumer_tree rejecting fusion when fusedConsumerWork > consumerWork * 1.02 (i.e. accept false) — this preserves default and rejects the bad ~1.06 case per-consumer.

Six distinct selective policies varying consumer thresholds and structure: e.g. thresholds 1.0, 1.02, 1.05, plus trees with size guards. Also can include aggregate in selective? Selective kind has tree and consumer_tree; aggregate tree gates whether selective evaluation applies. Keep aggregate permissive (threshold 2) so consumer tree decides? But "preserve default aggregate behavior when possible" — but selective policies presumably bypass aggregate? Safer: aggregate tree rejecting the bad case and consumer_tree variants exploring per-consumer granularity.

Six variants:
1. consumer threshold 1.02 flat, aggregate permissive (threshold 2).
2. consumer threshold 1.0 flat, aggregate permissive.
3. consumer threshold 1.05 flat, aggregate 2.
4. consumer tree: if producerElements small (<4096) accept else threshold 1.02; aggregate permissive.
5. consumer tree: if consumerWork large reject? Use consumerWork < 1000000 then accept else threshold 1.02. Aggregate 2.
6. mixed: aggregate 1.02 with consumer_tree that re-accepts fusedConsumerWork <= consumerWork*1.02 (redundant but distinct), actually make consumer accept-all (threshold 2) with aggregate 1.02 — union, distinct.

Submit all six.

content.text: All training decisions are single-consumer (`consumerCount=1`), and the only default-rejected case is a ratio of ~1.06 (17549136/17254224). So selective per-consumer fusion should mostly mirror the default, with the consumer tree handling small growth rather than tightening the aggregate. I'll propose six distinct selective variants with a permissive aggregate (2.0) letting the consumer tree decide, plus one union variant.
